### ⚑ Section 1 · Q1 · 1) — 2 marks

> Where do we drop our letters to be sent? Who delivers letters to our home?

- **Answer: We drop our letters in a postbox (letter box). The postman delivers letters to our home.**
- Answer points:
  - Postbox / letter box (also accept: at the post office) (1 mark)
  - Postman (postwoman, dakiya, mail carrier) (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Both parts right: postbox (or post office) and postman.
  - partial (1 mark): One part right.
  - none (0 marks): Neither part right.
- Model answer: We drop our letters in the postbox. The postman delivers letters to our home.
- Source: Ch 2 (deev102), p.2 l.4-22
- Teacher note: Both answers are in the textbook. "Post office" for the first part is accepted (letters can be posted there), which is a judgement call, so this item is ⚑ like the other picture items in Q1.

### ⚑ Section 1 · Q1 · 2) — 2 marks

> Identify this bird and write its name. What does this bird have to catch its prey?

- **Answer: Eagle. It has sharp claws (talons) and a sharp, curved beak to catch its prey.**
- Answer points:
  - Eagle (also accept: chil / garud; hawk, kite or falcon — the parent decides, see note) (1 mark)
  - Sharp claws (talons) and/or a sharp, curved (hooked) beak (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Names the eagle and says it has sharp claws or a sharp curved beak.
  - partial (1 mark): Only one part right (e.g. bird named but no feature, or "sharp claws" with a wrong bird).
  - none (0 marks): Neither part right.
- Model answer: This is an eagle. It has sharp claws and a sharp, curved beak to catch its prey.
- Source: Ch 3 (deev103), p.13 l.16-22
- Teacher note: The textbook says an eagle has "a sharp, curved beak and sharp claws to catch its prey", so either feature (or both) earns the second mark. Hawk, kite and falcon look very like an eagle; the drawing (white head, hooked yellow beak, big talons) is an eagle, but give the mark for "bird of prey"/hawk/kite if the parent feels the child recognised the kind of bird.

### ⚑ Section 1 · Q1 · 3) — 2 marks

> What kind of food group is this? Name any two food items from this group.

- **Answer: Energy-giving foods. Any two of: rice, potato, sweet potato, honey, banana, maize (corn), wheat, millets, apple, butter, ghee, oil.**
- Answer points:
  - Energy-giving foods (energy-rich / energy foods / carbohydrates) (1 mark)
  - Any two energy-giving foods, ½ each (rice, potato, sweet potato, honey, banana, maize/corn, wheat, millets, jaggery, sugar, butter, ghee, oil) (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Says energy-giving food and names two energy-giving foods.
  - partial (1 mark): Food group right but foods wrong or missing, or two correct foods without the group; ½ for one correct food.
  - none (0 marks): Group wrong and no correct food.
- Model answer: This is the energy-giving food group. Rice and potato are energy-giving foods.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.9 l.1-6
- Teacher note: "Carbohydrates" is not a textbook word but means the same here; accept it. The two foods may be named from the picture or from memory.

### ⚑ Section 1 · Q1 · 4) — 2 marks

> Name the person who mends wall using bricks and cement called? Write the name of any one tool which is used for building walls.

- **Answer: Mason (raj mistri). Tool: trowel (karni).**
- Answer points:
  - Mason (raj mistri, mistri, bricklayer, construction worker) (1 mark)
  - Any one tool: trowel (karni), spirit level, plumb line (sahul), hammer, shovel/spade, measuring tape, chisel, cement pan (tasla) (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Mason and one correct building tool.
  - partial (1 mark): Only one part right.
  - none (0 marks): Neither part right.
- Model answer: The person is called a mason. A trowel is used for building walls.
- Source: Ch 1 (deev101), p.8 l.5-13
- Teacher note: Printed as "Name the person who mends wall using bricks and cement called?" (two questions run together, and "wall" without "a"); kept as printed. The textbook example tool is the trowel, but any real wall-building tool gets the mark.

> Identify the device and write its name. Write any one benefit of using this device.

- Answer points:
  - Solar cooker (1 mark)
  - One benefit: uses free sunlight / saves gas, fuel or electricity / no smoke or ash, does not pollute / saves money (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Names the solar cooker and gives one correct benefit.
  - partial (1 mark): Only one part right.
  - none (0 marks): Neither part right.

### ⚑ Section 2 · Q6 · (a) — 1 mark

> I am an insect, green in colour. I have three pairs of legs, one pair of antennae to sense surroundings, also sometimes have two pairs of wings. Ans: \_\_\_\_\_\_

- **Answer: Grasshopper**
- Also accept: Grasshopper · grass hopper · Grasshoper · Grass-hopper · Tidda · Tiddi · Cricket · Praying mantis · Mantis · Katydid · Locust · grasshoppers · a grasshopper · green grasshopper · phadka · mitta · velukili
- Source: Ch 3 (deev103), p.17 l.2-8
- Teacher note: The clue copies the textbook lines about the grasshopper, so grasshopper is the key. A praying mantis, katydid, cricket or locust is also a green insect that fits every clue, so they are accepted. Printed "also sometimes have two pairs of wings" (no subject); kept as printed.

### ⚑ Section 2 · Q6 · (b) — 1 mark

> I am a small grain, round and grey. In winter roti, I make my way. Good for health and full of might, eat me to feel strong and bright. Ans: \_\_\_\_\_\_

- **Answer: Bajra (pearl millet)**
- Also accept: Bajra · Bajri · Bajre · Pearl millet · Pearl-millet · Sajje · Kambu · Kambu millet · Sajjalu · Bajra millet · Millet · Millets · bajara · kambam · cumbu · bajra roti
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.6 l.34-41
- Teacher note: The textbook says grandmother ate "jowar and bajra roti in winters"; bajra is the small round grey grain. "Millet" (the general name) is accepted too; jowar is a creamy-white grain, so it does not fit "grey". Because a general name is accepted, this item is ⚑.

### ⚑ Section 2 · Q8 · 1. — 1 mark

> Circle the one which does not belong to the group.

- Options: Ant · Wasp · Butterfly · Termite
- **Answer: Butterfly · Termite**
- Source: Ch 1 (deev101), p.10 l.9-17; Class 4 EVS content standard (not in textbook)
- Teacher note: All four are insects, so the textbook gives no single answer. Butterfly is the expected answer: ants, wasps and termites live together in colonies and bite or sting, while a butterfly lives alone and does neither. Termite is also defensible (it eats wood and is not related to the other three, which belong to the ant-and-bee family). Accept Butterfly or Termite if the child can give the reason.

### ⚑ Section 2 · Q8 · 3. — 1 mark

> Circle the one which does not belong to the group.

- Options: Marigold · Tulsi · Amla · Ajwain
- **Answer: Marigold · Amla**
- Source: Ch 4 (deev104), p.4 l.19-22; Ch 4 (deev104), p.7 l.13-19; Ch 5 (deev105), p.9 l.19-33
- Teacher note: Marigold is the expected answer: Tulsi, Amla and Ajwain are used as medicine or food, while marigold is a flower used for colour (natural dye). Amla is also defensible as the only fruit (Tulsi is a leaf, Ajwain a seed, Marigold a flower), so it is accepted too if the child gives that reason.

### ⚑ Section 2 · Q9 · 1. — 3 marks

> What is Van Mahotsav? When is it celebrated?

- **Answer: Van Mahotsav is the tree-planting festival. People plant trees to protect the environment and make the earth greener. It is celebrated every year in the rainy season, from 1 July to 7 July.**
- Answer points:
  - A festival of planting trees (tree-planting festival) (1 mark)
  - Why/what people do: plant trees to protect the environment, make the earth greener; clean parks (1 mark)
  - When: every year in the rainy season, 1 to 7 July (first week of July) (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (3 marks): Says it is a tree-planting festival, gives a purpose or activity, and gives the time (rainy season / 1–7 July).
  - partial (2 marks): Two of the three points.
  - weak (1 mark): One point only.
  - none (0 marks): No correct point.
- Model answer: Van Mahotsav is a festival of planting trees. People plant saplings to protect the environment and make the earth greener. It is celebrated every year from 1 July to 7 July, in the rainy season.
- Source: Ch 1 (deev101), p.6 l.1-12; Ch 1 (deev101), p.5 l.15-27

### ⚑ Section 2 · Q9 · 2. — 3 marks

> Who is a nature scientist? Write about its role.

- **Answer: A nature scientist is a person who studies plants and animals. Role: studies the features of plants and animals and how they depend on each other, guides people on nature trails, teaches us not to harm plants and animals, and helps protect and conserve nature.**
- Answer points:
  - A person who studies plants and animals (nature/wildlife) (1 mark)
  - Role (one point): studies features of plants and animals / how they depend on each other (1 mark)
  - Role (another point): guides us in exploring forests, teaches safety rules, makes sure we do not harm plants and animals, helps protect nature (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (3 marks): Correct meaning and two points about the role.
  - partial (2 marks): Correct meaning and one role point, or two role points without the meaning.
  - weak (1 mark): Only the meaning, or only one role point.
  - none (0 marks): No correct point.
- Model answer: A nature scientist is a person who studies plants and animals. Abha Didi guided the students in the forest. A nature scientist studies the features of plants and animals and teaches us to protect them and not harm them.
- Source: Ch 3 (deev103), p.4 l.5-14; Ch 3 (deev103), p.23 l.5
- Teacher note: Printed "Write about its role." ("its" for a person); kept as printed. The textbook only says a nature scientist "studies plants and animals" and shows Abha Didi guiding the trail and asking the students not to harm plants and animals; the role points are judged by the parent.

### ⚑ Section 2 · Q9 · 3. — 3 marks

> What is a balanced diet?

- **Answer: A balanced diet has food in the right quantities from all three food groups: protective foods (fruits and vegetables) the most, then body-building foods, and some energy-giving foods, with enough water. It keeps us healthy, active and happy.**
- Answer points:
  - Food from all the food groups, in the right quantities (1 mark)
  - Names the groups: energy-giving, body-building and protective foods (or examples of each) (1 mark)
  - Why: keeps us healthy, active and strong / helps balanced growth (or: protective foods the most, plus water) (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (3 marks): Explains food from all groups in the right amounts, names the groups, and says why it is needed.
  - partial (2 marks): Two of the three points.
  - weak (1 mark): One point (e.g. only "healthy food").
  - none (0 marks): No correct point.
- Model answer: A balanced diet is food that has all three food groups in the right amounts — energy-giving foods, body-building foods and protective foods (fruits and vegetables the most). It keeps us healthy, active and happy.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.11 l.25-30; Ch 5 (deev105), p.8 l.1-5

### ⚑ Section 2 · Q9 · 4. — 3 marks

> Write the full form of ATM. Write any two uses of ATM.

- **Answer: ATM stands for Automated Teller Machine. Uses (any two): to take out money at any time; to check the bank balance; to deposit cash (in some machines); to get a mini statement; to change the PIN; to transfer money.**
- Answer points:
  - Automated Teller Machine (also accept "Automatic Teller Machine") (1 mark)
  - Use 1, e.g. take out (withdraw) money any time (1 mark)
  - Use 2, e.g. check balance / deposit cash / mini statement / change PIN / transfer money (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (3 marks): Correct full form and two correct uses.
  - partial (2 marks): Two of the three points.
  - weak (1 mark): One point.
  - none (0 marks): No correct point.
- Model answer: ATM stands for Automated Teller Machine. We use it to take out money at any time, and to check how much money is in our bank account.
- Source: Ch 2 (deev102), p.8 l.4-8; Class 4 EVS content standard (not in textbook)
- Teacher note: The textbook gives one use ("take out money anytime we need it"); the second use comes from general knowledge, so any real ATM use counts. "Any Time Money" is a common wrong guess and gets no mark for the full form.

### ⚑ Section 2 · Q9 · 5. — 3 marks

> What is Gond art? How are the paints made to make Gond art?

- **Answer: Gond art is a tribal form of painting on walls using natural colours; the artists paint pictures of nature such as trees, animals, birds and humans. The paints are made from natural things: extracts of flowers, leaves (and bark and roots) and powdered coloured stones, e.g. by boiling plant parts in water and straining the coloured liquid.**
- Answer points:
  - Gond art: a (tribal) painting on walls using natural colours (1 mark)
  - It shows pictures of nature — trees, animals, birds, humans (1 mark)
  - Paints made from natural things: flowers, leaves, bark, roots, coloured stones powdered (or boiled and strained) (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (3 marks): Explains what Gond art is, what it shows, and how natural paints are made.
  - partial (2 marks): Two of the three points.
  - weak (1 mark): One point.
  - none (0 marks): No correct point.
- Model answer: Gond art is a painting on walls made with natural colours. It shows trees, animals, birds and people. The paints are made from flowers, leaves and powdered coloured stones.
- Source: Ch 4 (deev104), p.4 l.5-29
- Teacher note: The textbook describes Gond art in a "Do you know?" box and, on the same page, says grandmother’s paint "was made of natural extracts of flowers, leaves and with the powdered coloured stones"; it does not say these are the Gond paints in so many words, so the parent judges the paint point (natural dye made by boiling plant parts is also accepted).

### ⚑ Section 3 · Q12 · 1. — 2 marks

> What is super food? Write the names of any two super food.

- **Answer: Super foods are foods that are very rich in nutrients and keep us healthy and strong, like millets. Any two: jowar, bajra, ragi, jau (barley), amla, other millets.**
- Answer points:
  - Meaning: food that is very rich in nutrients and very good for health (e.g. millets) (1 mark)
  - Any two super foods, ½ each: jowar, bajra, ragi, jau/barley, kodo, foxtail millet, amla, moringa, spinach, nuts, sprouts (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Correct meaning and two correct super foods.
  - partial (1 mark): Meaning only, or two foods only; ½ for one correct food.
  - none (0 marks): Nothing correct.
- Model answer: Super foods are foods that are very rich in nutrients and keep us healthy. Jowar and ragi are super foods.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.6 l.34-41
- Teacher note: Printed "Answers the following questions." (block heading) and "any two super food" (singular); both kept as printed. The textbook does not define super food; it shows a "Super Food" stall of millets, which "are rich sources of nutrients". Other nutrient-rich foods (amla, moringa, nuts) are accepted.

### ⚑ Section 3 · Q12 · 2. — 2 marks

> What things should be kept in a first-aid box?

- **Answer: Any four of: bandages, cotton, antiseptic liquid or cream, medicines (for fever, pain, stomach ache), mosquito repellent cream, scissors, plaster/band-aid, thermometer, gauze, ointment for burns.**
- Answer points:
  - Two correct things, ½ each (e.g. bandage, cotton) (1 mark)
  - Two more correct things, ½ each (e.g. antiseptic cream, medicines, mosquito repellent cream, scissors, thermometer) (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Four correct first-aid things.
  - partial (1 mark): Two or three correct things (½ each).
  - none (0 marks): None or one correct thing.
- Model answer: A first-aid box should have bandages, cotton, antiseptic cream, some medicines and scissors.
- Source: Ch 4 (deev104), p.7 l.6-9; Ch 4 (deev104), p.7 l.20
- Teacher note: Marks are 2 for a list question, so ½ per correct item (four needed) is used. The textbook mentions medicines and mosquito repellent cream; the other items come from general knowledge.

### ⚑ Section 3 · Q13 · 1. — 2 marks

> Different plants and animals are dependent on each other.

- **Answer: Animals depend on plants for food, shelter and oxygen; plants depend on animals to spread their seeds and pollen, and animal waste makes the soil fertile. Everything in nature is connected (web of life), so if one part disappears the others suffer.**
- Answer points:
  - Animals depend on plants (food, shelter, oxygen) (1 mark)
  - Plants depend on animals (pollination, spreading seeds, manure) / everything in nature is connected, so losing one affects others (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Gives how animals need plants and how plants need animals (or the web-of-life idea).
  - partial (1 mark): Only one direction of dependence.
  - none (0 marks): No correct reason.
- Model answer: Animals need plants for food and shelter, and plants need animals to spread their seeds and pollen. In nature everything is connected, so they depend on each other.
- Source: Ch 3 (deev103), p.20 l.12-16; Ch 3 (deev103), p.22 l.1-16

### ⚑ Section 3 · Q13 · 2. — 2 marks

> We should avoid eating junk food.

- **Answer: Junk food has a lot of oil, salt and sugar and very few nutrients, so eating it regularly or in large amounts is not healthy; it can cause weight gain, stomach problems, tooth decay and illness. Fresh home-cooked food is better.**
- Answer points:
  - Junk food has too much oil, salt or sugar (and few nutrients) / is over-processed (1 mark)
  - It harms health: makes us unhealthy, fat, ill, weak teeth, stomach problems / home-cooked food is better (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Says what is in junk food and how it harms health.
  - partial (1 mark): Only one of the two points.
  - none (0 marks): No correct reason.
- Model answer: Junk food has a lot of oil, salt and sugar. Eating it often makes us unhealthy and ill, so fresh home-cooked food is better.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.10 l.1-11

### ⚑ Section 3 · Q13 · 3. — 2 marks

> Drinking sufficient water should be a part of our healthy habits.

- **Answer: Water helps in digesting food and keeps our skin and body healthy; it removes waste from our body through urine, sweat and faeces. So we must drink enough water every day.**
- Answer points:
  - Water helps digest food / keeps skin and body healthy (1 mark)
  - Water removes waste from the body (urine, sweat, faeces) / keeps the body cool and hydrated (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Two correct reasons why water is needed.
  - partial (1 mark): One correct reason.
  - none (0 marks): No correct reason.
- Model answer: Water helps us digest food and keeps our skin and body healthy. It also removes waste from our body through urine and sweat.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.12 l.7-17

### ⚑ Section 3 · Q14 — 5 marks

> Circle ten words related to food in the grid below.

- **Answer: HONEY, BAJRA, LEMON, BEANS, EGG, MANGO, OAT, CARROT, AMLA, TOFU (POTATO is the given example).**
- Answer points:
  - HONEY (0.5 marks)
  - BAJRA (0.5 marks)
  - LEMON (0.5 marks)
  - BEANS (0.5 marks)
  - EGG (0.5 marks)
  - MANGO (0.5 marks)
  - OAT (0.5 marks)
  - CARROT (0.5 marks)
  - AMLA (0.5 marks)
  - TOFU (0.5 marks)
- Rubric:
  - full (5 marks): Ten different food words circled correctly (not counting POTATO).
  - partial (2.5 marks): Some food words circled: ½ mark for each correct word (e.g. five words = 2½).
  - none (0 marks): No food word circled correctly.
- Model answer: HONEY, BAJRA, LEMON, BEANS, EGG, MANGO, OAT, CARROT, AMLA and TOFU are circled.
- Marking guide: Paper-based: ½ mark for each correctly circled food word, up to 10 words (5 marks). Where the words are — down: HONEY (column 1, rows 2–6), BAJRA (column 3, rows 1–5), LEMON (column 4, rows 1–5), EGG (column 7, rows 2–4), BEANS (column 9, rows 1–5), TOFU (column 8, rows 6–9); across: MANGO (row 6, columns 2–6), OAT (row 6, columns 6–8), CARROT (row 7, columns 4–9), AMLA (row 8, columns 3–6). Also accept UPMA (down column 2, rows 4–7), OAT read down column 3 (rows 7–9), BEAN for BEANS, and NAAN (diagonal) — each is a real food word in the grid. Do not count the circled example POTATO as one of the ten. A circle that does not cover a whole word in a straight line gets no mark.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.9 l.1-33; Ch 5 (deev105), p.16 l.5-7
- Teacher note: The answer key was found by searching the grid (the teacher’s key is not printed). Exactly ten straight-line words besides the example were found, so POTATO, the given example, is not counted among the ten. TOFU shares the T and O of POTATO, and OAT is part of GOAT; both are still food words. The grid also hides UPMA (down column 2) and NAAN (diagonal), which are accepted as substitutes. Letters are copied from the page image (the text layer misplaces the P in row 2).

#### ⚑ Section 1 · Q1 · 1) — 2 marks

> Where do we drop our letters to be sent? Who delivers letters to our home?

- **Answer: We drop our letters in a postbox (letter box). The postman delivers letters to our home.**
- Answer points:
  - Postbox / letter box (also accept: at the post office) (1 mark)
  - Postman (postwoman, dakiya, mail carrier) (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Both parts right: postbox (or post office) and postman.
  - partial (1 mark): One part right.
  - none (0 marks): Neither part right.
- Model answer: We drop our letters in the postbox. The postman delivers letters to our home.
- Source: Ch 2 (deev102), p.2 l.4-22
- Teacher note: Both answers are in the textbook. "Post office" for the first part is accepted (letters can be posted there), which is a judgement call, so this item is ⚑ like the other picture items in Q1.

#### ⚑ Section 1 · Q1 · 2) — 2 marks

> Identify this bird and write its name. What does this bird have to catch its prey?

- **Answer: Eagle. It has sharp claws (talons) and a sharp, curved beak to catch its prey.**
- Answer points:
  - Eagle (also accept: chil / garud; hawk, kite or falcon — the parent decides, see note) (1 mark)
  - Sharp claws (talons) and/or a sharp, curved (hooked) beak (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Names the eagle and says it has sharp claws or a sharp curved beak.
  - partial (1 mark): Only one part right (e.g. bird named but no feature, or "sharp claws" with a wrong bird).
  - none (0 marks): Neither part right.
- Model answer: This is an eagle. It has sharp claws and a sharp, curved beak to catch its prey.
- Source: Ch 3 (deev103), p.13 l.16-22
- Teacher note: The textbook says an eagle has "a sharp, curved beak and sharp claws to catch its prey", so either feature (or both) earns the second mark. Hawk, kite and falcon look very like an eagle; the drawing (white head, hooked yellow beak, big talons) is an eagle, but give the mark for "bird of prey"/hawk/kite if the parent feels the child recognised the kind of bird.

#### ⚑ Section 1 · Q1 · 3) — 2 marks

> What kind of food group is this? Name any two food items from this group.

- **Answer: Energy-giving foods. Any two of: rice, potato, sweet potato, honey, banana, maize (corn), wheat, millets, apple, butter, ghee, oil.**
- Answer points:
  - Energy-giving foods (energy-rich / energy foods / carbohydrates) (1 mark)
  - Any two energy-giving foods, ½ each (rice, potato, sweet potato, honey, banana, maize/corn, wheat, millets, jaggery, sugar, butter, ghee, oil) (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Says energy-giving food and names two energy-giving foods.
  - partial (1 mark): Food group right but foods wrong or missing, or two correct foods without the group; ½ for one correct food.
  - none (0 marks): Group wrong and no correct food.
- Model answer: This is the energy-giving food group. Rice and potato are energy-giving foods.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.9 l.1-6
- Teacher note: "Carbohydrates" is not a textbook word but means the same here; accept it. The two foods may be named from the picture or from memory.

#### ⚑ Section 1 · Q1 · 4) — 2 marks

> Name the person who mends wall using bricks and cement called? Write the name of any one tool which is used for building walls.

- **Answer: Mason (raj mistri). Tool: trowel (karni).**
- Answer points:
  - Mason (raj mistri, mistri, bricklayer, construction worker) (1 mark)
  - Any one tool: trowel (karni), spirit level, plumb line (sahul), hammer, shovel/spade, measuring tape, chisel, cement pan (tasla) (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Mason and one correct building tool.
  - partial (1 mark): Only one part right.
  - none (0 marks): Neither part right.
- Model answer: The person is called a mason. A trowel is used for building walls.
- Source: Ch 1 (deev101), p.8 l.5-13
- Teacher note: Printed as "Name the person who mends wall using bricks and cement called?" (two questions run together, and "wall" without "a"); kept as printed. The textbook example tool is the trowel, but any real wall-building tool gets the mark.

#### ⚑ Section 1 · Q1 · 5) — 2 marks

- **Answer: Solar cooker. Benefit: it cooks food using sunlight, so it saves fuel/gas/electricity and does not pollute the air with smoke or ash.**
- Answer points:

- **Answer: Bajra (pearl millet)**
- Also accept: Bajra · Bajri · Bajre · Pearl millet · Pearl-millet · Sajje · Kambu · Kambu millet · Sajjalu · Bajra millet · Millet · Millets · bajara · kambam · cumbu · bajra roti
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.6 l.34-41
- Teacher note: The textbook says grandmother ate "jowar and bajra roti in winters"; bajra is the small round grey grain. "Millet" (the general name) is accepted too; jowar is a creamy-white grain, so it does not fit "grey". Because a general name is accepted, this item is ⚑.

**Q8 — Circle the one which does not belong to the group. ( 4 x 1 = 4)**

#### ⚑ Section 2 · Q8 · 1. — 1 mark

> Circle the one which does not belong to the group.

- Options: Ant · Wasp · Butterfly · Termite
- **Answer: Butterfly · Termite**
- Source: Ch 1 (deev101), p.10 l.9-17; Class 4 EVS content standard (not in textbook)
- Teacher note: All four are insects, so the textbook gives no single answer. Butterfly is the expected answer: ants, wasps and termites live together in colonies and bite or sting, while a butterfly lives alone and does neither. Termite is also defensible (it eats wood and is not related to the other three, which belong to the ant-and-bee family). Accept Butterfly or Termite if the child can give the reason.

#### Section 2 · Q8 · 2. — 1 mark

> Circle the one which does not belong to the group.

- Options: School · Playground · Hospital · Kitchen
- **Answer: Kitchen**
- Source: Ch 1 (deev101), p.5 l.8-11

#### ⚑ Section 2 · Q8 · 3. — 1 mark

> Circle the one which does not belong to the group.

- Options: Marigold · Tulsi · Amla · Ajwain
- **Answer: Marigold · Amla**
- Source: Ch 4 (deev104), p.4 l.19-22; Ch 4 (deev104), p.7 l.13-19; Ch 5 (deev105), p.9 l.19-33
- Teacher note: Marigold is the expected answer: Tulsi, Amla and Ajwain are used as medicine or food, while marigold is a flower used for colour (natural dye). Amla is also defensible as the only fruit (Tulsi is a leaf, Ajwain a seed, Marigold a flower), so it is accepted too if the child gives that reason.

#### Section 2 · Q8 · 4. — 1 mark

> Circle the one which does not belong to the group.

- Options: Chips · Idli · Burger · Pizza
- **Answer: Idli**

**Q9 — Answer the following questions. (5×3=15)**

#### ⚑ Section 2 · Q9 · 1. — 3 marks

> What is Van Mahotsav? When is it celebrated?

- **Answer: Van Mahotsav is the tree-planting festival. People plant trees to protect the environment and make the earth greener. It is celebrated every year in the rainy season, from 1 July to 7 July.**
- Answer points:
  - A festival of planting trees (tree-planting festival) (1 mark)
  - Why/what people do: plant trees to protect the environment, make the earth greener; clean parks (1 mark)
  - When: every year in the rainy season, 1 to 7 July (first week of July) (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (3 marks): Says it is a tree-planting festival, gives a purpose or activity, and gives the time (rainy season / 1–7 July).
  - partial (2 marks): Two of the three points.
  - weak (1 mark): One point only.
  - none (0 marks): No correct point.
- Model answer: Van Mahotsav is a festival of planting trees. People plant saplings to protect the environment and make the earth greener. It is celebrated every year from 1 July to 7 July, in the rainy season.
- Source: Ch 1 (deev101), p.6 l.1-12; Ch 1 (deev101), p.5 l.15-27

#### ⚑ Section 2 · Q9 · 2. — 3 marks

> Who is a nature scientist? Write about its role.

- **Answer: A nature scientist is a person who studies plants and animals. Role: studies the features of plants and animals and how they depend on each other, guides people on nature trails, teaches us not to harm plants and animals, and helps protect and conserve nature.**
- Answer points:
  - A person who studies plants and animals (nature/wildlife) (1 mark)
  - Role (one point): studies features of plants and animals / how they depend on each other (1 mark)
  - Role (another point): guides us in exploring forests, teaches safety rules, makes sure we do not harm plants and animals, helps protect nature (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (3 marks): Correct meaning and two points about the role.
  - partial (2 marks): Correct meaning and one role point, or two role points without the meaning.
  - weak (1 mark): Only the meaning, or only one role point.
  - none (0 marks): No correct point.
- Model answer: A nature scientist is a person who studies plants and animals. Abha Didi guided the students in the forest. A nature scientist studies the features of plants and animals and teaches us to protect them and not harm them.
- Source: Ch 3 (deev103), p.4 l.5-14; Ch 3 (deev103), p.23 l.5
- Teacher note: Printed "Write about its role." ("its" for a person); kept as printed. The textbook only says a nature scientist "studies plants and animals" and shows Abha Didi guiding the trail and asking the students not to harm plants and animals; the role points are judged by the parent.

#### ⚑ Section 2 · Q9 · 3. — 3 marks

> What is a balanced diet?

- **Answer: A balanced diet has food in the right quantities from all three food groups: protective foods (fruits and vegetables) the most, then body-building foods, and some energy-giving foods, with enough water. It keeps us healthy, active and happy.**
- Answer points:
  - Food from all the food groups, in the right quantities (1 mark)
  - Names the groups: energy-giving, body-building and protective foods (or examples of each) (1 mark)
  - Why: keeps us healthy, active and strong / helps balanced growth (or: protective foods the most, plus water) (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (3 marks): Explains food from all groups in the right amounts, names the groups, and says why it is needed.
  - partial (2 marks): Two of the three points.
  - weak (1 mark): One point (e.g. only "healthy food").
  - none (0 marks): No correct point.
- Model answer: A balanced diet is food that has all three food groups in the right amounts — energy-giving foods, body-building foods and protective foods (fruits and vegetables the most). It keeps us healthy, active and happy.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.11 l.25-30; Ch 5 (deev105), p.8 l.1-5

#### ⚑ Section 2 · Q9 · 4. — 3 marks

> Write the full form of ATM. Write any two uses of ATM.

- **Answer: ATM stands for Automated Teller Machine. Uses (any two): to take out money at any time; to check the bank balance; to deposit cash (in some machines); to get a mini statement; to change the PIN; to transfer money.**
- Answer points:
  - Automated Teller Machine (also accept "Automatic Teller Machine") (1 mark)
  - Use 1, e.g. take out (withdraw) money any time (1 mark)
  - Use 2, e.g. check balance / deposit cash / mini statement / change PIN / transfer money (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (3 marks): Correct full form and two correct uses.
  - partial (2 marks): Two of the three points.
  - weak (1 mark): One point.
  - none (0 marks): No correct point.
- Model answer: ATM stands for Automated Teller Machine. We use it to take out money at any time, and to check how much money is in our bank account.
- Source: Ch 2 (deev102), p.8 l.4-8; Class 4 EVS content standard (not in textbook)
- Teacher note: The textbook gives one use ("take out money anytime we need it"); the second use comes from general knowledge, so any real ATM use counts. "Any Time Money" is a common wrong guess and gets no mark for the full form.

#### ⚑ Section 2 · Q9 · 5. — 3 marks

> What is Gond art? How are the paints made to make Gond art?

- **Answer: Gond art is a tribal form of painting on walls using natural colours; the artists paint pictures of nature such as trees, animals, birds and humans. The paints are made from natural things: extracts of flowers, leaves (and bark and roots) and powdered coloured stones, e.g. by boiling plant parts in water and straining the coloured liquid.**
- Answer points:
  - Gond art: a (tribal) painting on walls using natural colours (1 mark)
  - It shows pictures of nature — trees, animals, birds, humans (1 mark)
  - Paints made from natural things: flowers, leaves, bark, roots, coloured stones powdered (or boiled and strained) (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (3 marks): Explains what Gond art is, what it shows, and how natural paints are made.
  - partial (2 marks): Two of the three points.
  - weak (1 mark): One point.
  - none (0 marks): No correct point.
- Model answer: Gond art is a painting on walls made with natural colours. It shows trees, animals, birds and people. The paints are made from flowers, leaves and powdered coloured stones.
- Source: Ch 4 (deev104), p.4 l.5-29
- Teacher note: The textbook describes Gond art in a "Do you know?" box and, on the same page, says grandmother’s paint "was made of natural extracts of flowers, leaves and with the powdered coloured stones"; it does not say these are the Gond paints in so many words, so the parent judges the paint point (natural dye made by boiling plant parts is also accepted).

**Q10 — Compare between communication in earlier times and communication in present time on the following points. (1x5=5)**

#### ⚑ Section 2 · Q10 — 1 mark

> Type of communication

- **Answer: Earlier times: letters, telegram, messengers, pigeons, drumbeats. Present time: mobile phones, internet, email, text messages, video calls, social media.**
- Answer points:
  - Earlier times — letters, telegram, messengers, pigeons, drumbeats (0.5 marks)
  - Present time — mobile phones, internet, email, text messages, video calls, social media (0.5 marks)
- Rubric:
  - full (1 mark): A sensible entry in both cells (earlier and present).
  - partial (0.5 marks): A sensible entry in one cell only.
  - none (0 marks): Neither cell sensible.
- Model answer: Earlier: letters, telegram, messengers, pigeons, drumbeats. Present: mobile phones, internet, email, text messages, video calls, social media.
- Source: Ch 2 (deev102), p.4 l.1-31; Ch 2 (deev102), p.3 l.5-25
- Teacher note: In print, "earlier times" and "present time" in the instruction are bold, italic and underlined; underlining can only be shown on an item’s question here, so it is not shown. Q10 is an open comparison table: any sensible entry in each cell gets ½ mark.

#### ⚑ Section 2 · Q10 — 1 mark

> Speed of communication

- **Answer: Earlier times: slow; letters took days or weeks to reach. Present time: very fast; messages reach in seconds.**
- Answer points:
  - Earlier times — slow; letters took days or weeks to reach (0.5 marks)
  - Present time — very fast; messages reach in seconds (0.5 marks)
- Rubric:
  - full (1 mark): A sensible entry in both cells (earlier and present).
  - partial (0.5 marks): A sensible entry in one cell only.
  - none (0 marks): Neither cell sensible.
- Model answer: Earlier: slow. Present: very fast.
- Source: Ch 2 (deev102), p.4 l.1-31; Ch 2 (deev102), p.3 l.5-25

#### ⚑ Section 2 · Q10 — 1 mark

> Frequency of communication

- **Answer: Earlier times: less often; people wrote letters only now and then. Present time: very often; people talk or message every day, many times a day.**
- Answer points:
  - Earlier times — less often; people wrote letters only now and then (0.5 marks)
  - Present time — very often; people talk or message every day, many times a day (0.5 marks)
- Rubric:
  - full (1 mark): A sensible entry in both cells (earlier and present).
  - partial (0.5 marks): A sensible entry in one cell only.
  - none (0 marks): Neither cell sensible.
- Model answer: Earlier: less often. Present: very often.
- Source: Ch 2 (deev102), p.4 l.1-31; Ch 2 (deev102), p.3 l.5-25

#### ⚑ Section 2 · Q10 — 1 mark

> Language of communication

- **Answer: Earlier times: formal, written language in letters (often the local language). Present time: informal and short language, many languages, emojis and short forms.**
- Answer points:
  - Earlier times — formal, written language in letters (often the local language) (0.5 marks)
  - Present time — informal and short language, many languages, emojis and short forms (0.5 marks)
- Rubric:
  - full (1 mark): A sensible entry in both cells (earlier and present).
  - partial (0.5 marks): A sensible entry in one cell only.
  - none (0 marks): Neither cell sensible.
- Model answer: Earlier: formal, written language in letters (often the local language). Present: informal and short language, many languages, emojis and short forms.
- Source: Ch 2 (deev102), p.4 l.1-31; Ch 2 (deev102), p.3 l.5-25

#### ⚑ Section 2 · Q10 — 1 mark

> Challenges faced

- **Answer: Earlier times: letters got delayed or lost; long wait for a reply; messengers had to travel far. Present time: wrong information spreads fast; need network/internet and electricity; too much screen time; online fraud.**
- Answer points:
  - Earlier times — letters got delayed or lost; long wait for a reply; messengers had to travel far (0.5 marks)
  - Present time — wrong information spreads fast; need network/internet and electricity; too much screen time; online fraud (0.5 marks)
- Rubric:
  - full (1 mark): A sensible entry in both cells (earlier and present).
  - partial (0.5 marks): A sensible entry in one cell only.
  - none (0 marks): Neither cell sensible.
- Model answer: Earlier: letters got delayed or lost. Present: wrong information spreads fast.
- Source: Ch 2 (deev102), p.4 l.1-31; Ch 2 (deev102), p.3 l.5-25

**Q12 — Answers the following questions. ( 2 x 2 = 4)**

#### ⚑ Section 3 · Q12 · 1. — 2 marks

> What is super food? Write the names of any two super food.

- **Answer: Super foods are foods that are very rich in nutrients and keep us healthy and strong, like millets. Any two: jowar, bajra, ragi, jau (barley), amla, other millets.**
- Answer points:
  - Meaning: food that is very rich in nutrients and very good for health (e.g. millets) (1 mark)
  - Any two super foods, ½ each: jowar, bajra, ragi, jau/barley, kodo, foxtail millet, amla, moringa, spinach, nuts, sprouts (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Correct meaning and two correct super foods.
  - partial (1 mark): Meaning only, or two foods only; ½ for one correct food.
  - none (0 marks): Nothing correct.
- Model answer: Super foods are foods that are very rich in nutrients and keep us healthy. Jowar and ragi are super foods.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.6 l.34-41
- Teacher note: Printed "Answers the following questions." (block heading) and "any two super food" (singular); both kept as printed. The textbook does not define super food; it shows a "Super Food" stall of millets, which "are rich sources of nutrients". Other nutrient-rich foods (amla, moringa, nuts) are accepted.

#### ⚑ Section 3 · Q12 · 2. — 2 marks

> What things should be kept in a first-aid box?

- **Answer: Any four of: bandages, cotton, antiseptic liquid or cream, medicines (for fever, pain, stomach ache), mosquito repellent cream, scissors, plaster/band-aid, thermometer, gauze, ointment for burns.**
- Answer points:
  - Two correct things, ½ each (e.g. bandage, cotton) (1 mark)
  - Two more correct things, ½ each (e.g. antiseptic cream, medicines, mosquito repellent cream, scissors, thermometer) (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Four correct first-aid things.
  - partial (1 mark): Two or three correct things (½ each).
  - none (0 marks): None or one correct thing.
- Model answer: A first-aid box should have bandages, cotton, antiseptic cream, some medicines and scissors.
- Source: Ch 4 (deev104), p.7 l.6-9; Ch 4 (deev104), p.7 l.20
- Teacher note: Marks are 2 for a list question, so ½ per correct item (four needed) is used. The textbook mentions medicines and mosquito repellent cream; the other items come from general knowledge.

**Q13 — Give reason. ( 3 x 2 = 6 )**

#### ⚑ Section 3 · Q13 · 1. — 2 marks

> Different plants and animals are dependent on each other.

- **Answer: Animals depend on plants for food, shelter and oxygen; plants depend on animals to spread their seeds and pollen, and animal waste makes the soil fertile. Everything in nature is connected (web of life), so if one part disappears the others suffer.**
- Answer points:
  - Animals depend on plants (food, shelter, oxygen) (1 mark)
  - Plants depend on animals (pollination, spreading seeds, manure) / everything in nature is connected, so losing one affects others (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Gives how animals need plants and how plants need animals (or the web-of-life idea).
  - partial (1 mark): Only one direction of dependence.
  - none (0 marks): No correct reason.
- Model answer: Animals need plants for food and shelter, and plants need animals to spread their seeds and pollen. In nature everything is connected, so they depend on each other.
- Source: Ch 3 (deev103), p.20 l.12-16; Ch 3 (deev103), p.22 l.1-16

#### ⚑ Section 3 · Q13 · 2. — 2 marks

> We should avoid eating junk food.

- **Answer: Junk food has a lot of oil, salt and sugar and very few nutrients, so eating it regularly or in large amounts is not healthy; it can cause weight gain, stomach problems, tooth decay and illness. Fresh home-cooked food is better.**
- Answer points:
  - Junk food has too much oil, salt or sugar (and few nutrients) / is over-processed (1 mark)
  - It harms health: makes us unhealthy, fat, ill, weak teeth, stomach problems / home-cooked food is better (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Says what is in junk food and how it harms health.
  - partial (1 mark): Only one of the two points.
  - none (0 marks): No correct reason.
- Model answer: Junk food has a lot of oil, salt and sugar. Eating it often makes us unhealthy and ill, so fresh home-cooked food is better.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.10 l.1-11

#### ⚑ Section 3 · Q13 · 3. — 2 marks

> Drinking sufficient water should be a part of our healthy habits.

- **Answer: Water helps in digesting food and keeps our skin and body healthy; it removes waste from our body through urine, sweat and faeces. So we must drink enough water every day.**
- Answer points:
  - Water helps digest food / keeps skin and body healthy (1 mark)
  - Water removes waste from the body (urine, sweat, faeces) / keeps the body cool and hydrated (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Two correct reasons why water is needed.
  - partial (1 mark): One correct reason.
  - none (0 marks): No correct reason.
- Model answer: Water helps us digest food and keeps our skin and body healthy. It also removes waste from our body through urine and sweat.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.12 l.7-17

  - partial (0.5 marks): Correct area but marked untidily across a border, or marked but not named.
  - none (0 marks): Wrong state or not marked.
- Marking guide: Paper-based: the child marks and names Andhra Pradesh on the printed map; the parent checks against the answer-key map (shaded light green). Andhra Pradesh is on the south-east coast (Bay of Bengal), south of Odisha and Telangana and north of Tamil Nadu. Telangana (inland, north-west of it) is a separate state; if the child marks Telangana, give no mark. 1 mark for the correct state, marked clearly; 0 for a wrong state.
